dataset.name: GATE Computer Science and Information Technology Syllabus

source.document: GATE 2027 Official Syllabus - Computer Science and Information Technology
source.extraction_policy: Syllabus statements are transcribed from the source document. Line wrapping is normalized; wording and listed concepts are retained.

subjects.name: Engineering Mathematics
syllabus_statements: Discrete Mathematics: Propositional and first order logic. Sets, relations, functions, partial orders and lattices. Monoids, Groups. Graphs: connectivity, matching, colouring. Combinatorics: counting, recurrence relations, generating functions.
Linear Algebra: Matrices, determinants, system of linear equations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, LU decomposition.
Calculus: Limits, continuity and differentiability, Maxima and minima, Mean value theorem, Integration.
Probability and Statistics: Random variables, Uniform, normal, exponential, Poisson and binomial distributions. Mean, median, mode and standard deviation. Conditional probability and Bayes theorem.

subjects.name: Digital Logic
syllabus_statements: Boolean algebra and minimization – algebraic technique, Karnaugh map, tabular method. Design of combinational and sequential circuits. Number representation and arithmetic (fixed and floating point).

subjects.name: Computer Organization and Architecture
syllabus_statements: Instruction set and addressing modes. Design of arithmetic and logic unit (ALU). Design of control unit – hardwired and microprogrammed. Memory interfacing and hierarchy: performance, cache memory mapping. I/O interface (interrupt and DMA). Instruction pipelining, pipeline hazards.

subjects.name: Programming and Data Structures
syllabus_statements: Programming in C. Recursion. Arrays, stacks, queues, linked lists, trees, binary search trees, binary heaps, graphs.

subjects.name: Algorithms
syllabus_statements: Searching, sorting, hashing. Asymptotic worst case time and space complexity. Algorithm design techniques: greedy, dynamic programming and divide-and-conquer. Graph traversals, minimum spanning trees, shortest paths.

subjects.name: Theory of Computation
syllabus_statements: Regular expressions and finite automata. Context-free grammars and push-down automata. Regular and context-free languages, pumping lemma. Turing machines and undecidability.

subjects.name: Compiler Design
syllabus_statements: Lexical analysis, parsing, syntax-directed translation. Runtime environments. Intermediate code generation. Local optimisation, Data flow analyses: constant propagation, liveness analysis, common sub expression elimination.

subjects.name: Operating System
syllabus_statements: System calls, processes, threads, inter-process communication, concurrency and synchronization. Deadlock. CPU and I/O scheduling. Memory management and virtual memory. File systems.

subjects.name: Databases
syllabus_statements: ER-model. Relational model: relational algebra, tuple calculus, SQL. Integrity constraints, normal forms. File organization, indexing (e.g., B and B+ trees). Transactions and concurrency control.

subjects.name: Computer Networks
syllabus_statements: Principles of Layering; Basics of switching (circuit, packet and virtual circuit) and performance metrics;

Data link layer: error detection, Medium Access Control, Ethernet; Distance vector and link state routing; IPv4 - Fragmentation, CIDR Notation, Network Address Translation; TCP- flow control and congestion control, socket API; DNS and HTTP.
